"an" "banana") (void-function (car (cdr e)))) (condition-case e (s-equals? "a" "a") (void-function (car (cdr e)))) (condition-case e (s-count-matches "a" "banana") (void-function (car (cdr e)))))
note: WHERE THE LOADED PACKAGE STOPS, which is the honest measure this phase owes and the demand signal the next one starts from. Eight representative calls, each catching `void-function' and answering the NAME that was missing rather than a message, so the record reads as a list of frontier names instead of a diagnostic. Emacs answers all eight: ("a-b-c" "bXnXnX" "ABC" "abab" "hi" t t 3). AT PHASE 24 kg answered the first four and stopped at three names on the other four -- ("a-b-c" "bXnXnX" "ABC" "abab" save-match-data string-match-p string-equal save-match-data) -- so the frontier had moved from the READER to the match-data surface. AT PHASE 25.2 it moved again: all three of those names landed, and kg now answers ("a-b-c" "bXnXnX" "ABC" "abab" "  hi  " t t count-matches). Seven of the eight agree; what is left is two gaps of different kinds. `s-count-matches' reaches `count-matches', a NAME kg does not bind. `s-trim' answers its argument UNCHANGED -- not an error -- because s.el asks for "\\`[ \t\n\r]+" and kg's regex engine does not know the \\` spelling, so `string-match' answers nil and s.el's own `if' takes the else branch. That second one is the more interesting signal: kg's `^' and `$' already MEAN what \\` and \\' mean (they anchor the whole subject), so the gap is two spellings rather than a semantics -- and it is SILENT, which is why the kg-side test asserts the untrimmed string as a value. `replace-match' is missing too and is masked by it. AT PHASE 26.2 the frontier CLOSED: the anchor spellings landed in the engine, `count-matches' and `replace-match' landed in the prelude, and kg answers all eight -- ("a-b-c" "bXnXnX" "ABC" "abab" "hi" t t 3), Emacs' own list. The four that worked from the start are not a coincidence either: `s-join' is `mapconcat' and `s-repeat' is a loop, both of which Phase 24 had to generalise anyway. What this case can no longer do is name a frontier, which is why the probe has to be re-run against a WIDER sample of the package to find the next one.
